sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than smooth: a 20.4% jump in FY2018 to $54.7 billion [F3][D92], a 22.4% collapse in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
The FY2023 peak reflected favorable price realization and higher sales volume, with dealer inventory rising about $2.1 billion during the year [P32].
North America carried the latest year, contributing 3.4pp of the 4.3% revenue growth on a 6.4% regional increase [D515][D463][D514].
North America sales rose on higher sales volume, mainly higher sales of equipment to end users, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P12].
Power & Energy was the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue and added 5.2pp, while Construction Industries at 37.1% subtracted 0.6pp [D757][D759][D764][D766].
Construction Industries fell 2% on unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 9.1% [D489][D481], and operating income fell 14.7% against a 4.3% revenue rise [D464][D463].
The FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][D1122].
The 3.7pp margin decline was driven by cost of revenue, which subtracted 4.2pp, as unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion largely reflected higher tariffs [D476][D490][P9].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin, with a 24.0% effective tax rate [F50][F30][D1168][D449].
The largest swing was FY2023, when the margin rose 6.0pp, with cost of revenue adding 5.8pp [D370][D384].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.16x window median [F80][F40][D450][D1158].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion, a 13.2% margin below the 13.4% peer median [F100][D469][D447][D1148].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, 1.25x D&A, and the FY2025 investing outflow reflected an increase in capital expenditures [F90][D470][D452][P3].
Operating cash flow still rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid, partly offset by lower profit before taxes [P4].
Net debt was $26.2 billion at FY2025, with net cash of -38.8% of revenue against a -59.4% peer median across three peers [D456][D457][D1170].
That comparison omits long-term debt due within one year, which is in no line of this pack and was $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][X180].
Buybacks and dividends of $7.9 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D458][D459][D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% ranks at the 100th percentile against a 23.3% peer median [D462][D1155][D1156].
Total debt and net cash omit long-term debt due within one year, reported at $7.1 billion in FY2025, so net debt is understated every year in the window [R7][X180][D455].
This is a data-quality gap that weakens any leverage conclusion drawn from the pack's net cash figures.
Net debt rose for a second year through FY2025, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 to $26.2 billion [R1][D350][D456].
The direction is real even if the level is incomplete, and it coincides with the tariff-driven profit decline.
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 comes from the proxy pay-versus-performance table, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to ratios but matters where precision is claimed.
If the FY2026 operating margin falls below the 14.3% window median, the tariff-driven cost pressure would be confirmed, in the FY2026 10-K [D1123].
If capex as a share of revenue stays above the 4.2% FY2025 level, the free-cash-flow margin would face continued pressure, in the FY2026 10-K [D446].
If net cash as a share of revenue rises above -38.8%, the two-year rise in net debt would reverse, in the FY2026 10-K [D457].
